items.title: AnyVar MCP Server
items.text:
MCP server for AnyVar.

  • Getting started: install the package, set up and verify AnyVar, and configure the MCP server.
  • Contributing: set up a development environment and contribute code or documentation.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: This page explains how to set up the project for development, run tests, and update the documentation.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
You will need:

  • Python 3.13 or newer
  • Git
  • A terminal or command prompt

items.title: Set up a virtual environment
items.text:
If you are not a repository maintainer, first fork the repository on GitHub. Then clone your fork (or the main repository if you have access), enter its directory, and create a virtual environment:

Replace OWNER with your GitHub username for a fork, or genomicmedlab for the main repository.

git clone https://github.com/OWNER/anyvar-mcp.git
cd anyvar-mcp
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

items.title: Install the development dependencies
items.text:
Install the package in editable mode with development, test, and documentation dependencies. Editable mode makes changes in src/ available without reinstalling:

python3 -m pip install -e '.[dev,tests,docs]'

items.title: Install the pre-commit hooks
items.text:
Install the hooks after installing the development dependencies:

prek install

items.title: Style checks
items.text:
Check style with ruff:

python3 -m ruff check --fix .
python3 -m ruff format .

items.title: Tests
items.text:
Run unit and integration tests:

python3 -m pytest

Mark tests that require a running AnyVar service or external resources with @pytest.mark.live.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
Edit the Markdown files in docs/. Preview the site locally:

zensical serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8001.

Build the site with the same strict checks used in CI:

zensical build --clean --strict

items.title: Open a pull request
items.text:
Run the checks relevant to your changes, review the generated documentation, and open a pull request on GitHub. Include a short summary of the change and any relevant testing or documentation notes.

If the pull request resolves an issue, say so with a closing keyword such as Closes #123, where 123 is the issue number. GitHub will close the issue automatically when the pull request merges. If the pull request is related to an issue but does not resolve it, use a non-closing reference such as Refs #123, where 123 is again the issue number, or link the issue through the pull request's GitHub interface instead.

items.title: AnyVar setup
items.text: This MCP server registers and retrieves variants through AnyVar's HTTP API. Follow AnyVar's setup instructions to start the required HTTP service, then use its URL to configure the MCP server.

items.title: Verifying the AnyVar service
items.text:
Check your AnyVar service before connecting the MCP server. Set ANYVAR_API_URL to your service's base URL; the example uses the local default. Run the remaining commands in the same terminal.

export ANYVAR_API_URL="http://localhost:8000"

items.title: Service info
items.text:
First, request service information to check that the service responds:

curl --fail-with-body "${ANYVAR_API_URL%/}/service-info" \
  | python3 -m json.tool --indent 2

Expected response excerpt:

{
  "id": "org.biocommons.anyvar",
  "name": "AnyVar",
  "type": {
    "group": "org.biocommons",
    "artifact": "anyvar",
    "version": "1.0.1.dev196+gec3c7651b"
  }
}

The full response also includes service metadata, supported data standards, and dependency information.

AnyVar version compatibility

This MCP server targets AnyVar commit ec3c765. Published releases and other commits may return different responses or lack endpoints used by this client, so the examples and client operations may fail or produce different results. Check your service's version in /service-info and use the linked commit for the behavior shown in this guide.

Ensure AnyVar service is running

If the request fails, check the URL and that the service is running. Open the service's base URL in a browser to view its API documentation.

items.title: Variant registration
items.text:
Register a sample variant to check processing and storage, and provide a record for the search below:

curl --fail-with-body --request PUT "${ANYVAR_API_URL%/}/variation" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"definition": "NC_000010.11:g.87894077C>T"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool --indent 2

Expected registration response:

{
  "input_variation": {
    "definition": "NC_000010.11:g.87894077C>T",
    "assembly_name": "GRCh38"
  },
  "messages": [],
  "object": {
    "id": "ga4gh:VA.K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
    "type": "Allele",
    "digest": "K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
    "location": {
      "id": "ga4gh:SL.01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
      "type": "SequenceLocation",
      "digest": "01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
      "sequenceReference": {
        "type": "SequenceReference",
        "refgetAccession": "SQ.ss8r_wB0-b9r44TQTMmVTI92884QvBiB"
      },
      "start": 87894076,
      "end": 87894077
    },
    "state": {
      "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
      "sequence": "T"
    }
  },
  "object_id": "ga4gh:VA.K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU"
}

items.title: Variant search
items.text:
Search the same interval to check that the registered variant can be retrieved:

curl --fail-with-body --get "${ANYVAR_API_URL%/}/variations" \
  --data-urlencode 'accession=ga4gh:SQ.ss8r_wB0-b9r44TQTMmVTI92884QvBiB' \
  --data-urlencode 'start=87894070' \
  --data-urlencode 'end=87894080' \
  | python3 -m json.tool --indent 2

Expected search response (your database may contain additional matches):

{
  "variations": [
    {
      "id": "ga4gh:VA.K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
      "type": "Allele",
      "digest": "K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
      "location": {
        "id": "ga4gh:SL.01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
        "type": "SequenceLocation",
        "digest": "01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
        "sequenceReference": {
          "type": "SequenceReference",
          "refgetAccession": "SQ.ss8r_wB0-b9r44TQTMmVTI92884QvBiB"
        },
        "start": 87894076,
        "end": 87894077
      },
      "state": {
        "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
        "sequence": "T"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJzdGFydCI6ODc4OTQwNzYsImlkIjoiZ2E0Z2g6VkEuSzdha3l6OVBIQjB3Zzh3Qk5WbFdBQWR2TWJKVUpKZlUifQ=="
}

The registered allele appears in variations.

items.title: MCP server configuration
items.text:
Set the AnyVar service URL, request timeout, and resource limits through environment variables or a .env file.

Configuration values are resolved in the following order of precedence (highest to lowest):

  1. Environment variables
  2. .env file

  3. Defaults

    • ANYVAR_API_URL: http://localhost:8000
    • ANYVAR_API_TIMEOUT: 10 seconds
    • ANYVAR_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE: 100 results (allowed range: 1–10,000)
    • ANYVAR_MAX_SEARCH_SPAN: 1000000 positions
    • ANYVAR_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES: 1048576 bytes (1 MiB)

Searches default to at most 100 variants per page to keep results manageable in conversations. Set ANYVAR_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE in the server's environment or .env file to change this default.

The separate 1 MiB response limit allows room for larger variants and explicitly requested larger pages while bounding how much data the client reads.

If a page exceeds the limit, lower ANYVAR_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE and restart the server before starting a new search. Keep the page size unchanged when following continuation cursors. Operators can raise ANYVAR_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES when larger responses are needed.

To configure values using a .env file, create one in the directory where you launch the MCP server:

ANYVAR_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
ANYVAR_API_TIMEOUT=10
ANYVAR_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE=100

To override a value for a single invocation, set the environment variable when launching the server. For example, to use a 15-second timeout:

ANYVAR_API_TIMEOUT=15 anyvar-mcp
